title: Mobility Equipment Retail Clause — Price Adjustment on a Cash-Sale Chair the Patient Keeps
content:
# Price Adjustment on a Cash-Sale Chair the Patient Keeps — Mobility Equipment

**Clause.** When a patient keeps a Mobility Equipment wheelchair Summit Ridge sold for cash after it needed a warranty repair in its first weeks, Summit Ridge returns part of the price as a price adjustment, worked out on the day it is booked from the chair's own sale line, service history and requests, and the patient accepts it in person. The price adjustment on a cash-sale chair the patient keeps is 5 percent of the price on its sale line plus a day credit of 1.00 for each day counted, the days running from the requested date of the chair's latest repair estimate request to its decision date (no days while that request is undecided or when the chair has none) and the day credit being that daily rate multiplied by those days, rounded to the cent half up; the adjustment is rounded to the cent half up and nothing else is added.

## The figure, step by step

1. Read the price (the sale amount) on the chair's cash sale line and take 5 percent of it.
2. Count the days from the requested date of the chair's latest repair estimate request (latest by requested date) to that request's decision date; no days while it is undecided, and none when the chair has no repair estimate request.
3. Day credit: those days multiplied by 1.00, rounded to the cent half up.
4. Add the two and round once, to the cent, half up. The delivery fee on the sale line plays no part.

## Worked examples (hypothetical sale lines and dates)

| Price on the sale line | Latest repair estimate request | Days | 5 percent of the price | Day credit | Price adjustment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 329.00 | requested 4 March, decided 12 March | 8 | 16.45 | 8.00 | 24.45 |
| 3995.00 | requested 4 March, undecided | 0 | 199.75 | 0.00 | 199.75 |
| 333.33 | requested 2 June, decided 5 June | 3 | 16.6665 | 3.00 | 19.67 |

## Basis Q&A

**On which day is it worked out?** On the day it is booked.

**Who accepts it?** The patient, in person.
